subject: Architecture
title: Green Roofs: Gardens in the Sky
description: Learn Green Roofs: Gardens in the Sky in one minute.

hook.text: A layer of plants on a roof can insulate, absorb rain, clean air, and cool the building below for free.

buildup.text: Green roofs range from thin sedum mats to full rooftop parks with trees, paths, and ponds.

discovery.text: They absorb up to 80% of rainfall, reducing storm drain flooding and filtering pollutants from runoff.

twist.text: Copenhagen requires green roofs on all new buildings with slopes under 30 degrees. It's law, not choice.

climax.text: Green roofs extend a roof's lifespan by 20-30 years by shielding it from UV radiation and temperature swings.

punchline.text: The roof protects the building. The garden protects the roof.

quiz.question: How much rainfall can a green roof absorb?

details.summary: Green roofs replace conventional roofing with layers of soil and vegetation that insulate buildings, absorb rainwater, reduce urban heat, filter air pollution, and provide habitat for wildlife.
details.whyItMatters: Green roofs solve multiple urban problems simultaneously — flooding, heat islands, air pollution, biodiversity loss, and building energy use. Their multi-benefit nature makes them one of the most cost-effective green infrastructure investments.
takeaways: Soil and vegetation replace conventional roofing materials
Retains 50-90% of rainfall, reducing urban storm water runoff
Reduces urban heat, insulates buildings, and supports wildlife

faq.question: Can any building support a green roof?
faq.answer: Most flat and low-slope roofs can be retrofitted with lightweight extensive green roofs (sedum mats weighing 60-150 kg per square meter when saturated). Intensive green roofs with deeper soil and larger plants require structural assessment.

faq.question: How much do green roofs cost compared to conventional roofs?
faq.answer: Green roofs cost 2-3 times more to install than conventional roofs but last twice as long by protecting the waterproof membrane from UV damage and temperature extremes. Over 40 years, the lifecycle cost is often lower when energy savings and reduced storm water fees are included.
